en: The Ritual Manual for the *Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī-sūtra* (After reciting the Great Compassion Mantra, sprinkle water for purification).
Śākyamuni Tathāgata, the Teacher who expounded this sūtra.
The Tathāgata Śikhin. The Tathāgata has descended to this Dharma assembly.
Venerable Ānanda, may you likewise bestow your protective grace. It is said:
Within the sandalwood forest, six *zhu* of its value outweigh all of Saha; within Anāthapiṇḍada’s garden, a single incense stick penetrates [the three realms].
Arriving at Vulture Peak, ancient cauldrons swirl with pure auspicious vapors; jade incense burners are encircled by azure auspicious clouds.
I now offer this at the place of fervor to the Tathāgata; I pray only that you will compassionately and piteously accept it. I look up and address you:
The Sage among Sages, the Lord of Gods among Gods, whose fame is universally renowned throughout the mundane and supramundane worlds;
the compassionate father who extracts one from the cycle of rebirth and rescues from suffering; the guiding teacher who benefits and brings joy across the ocean of karma.

Responding to vows like an echo in a valley, arriving at the call like the great sound returning with spring, he—the Tamer of the Five Regions and World-Hero of the Three Realms—has descended upon this site of practice to act as [the Buddha].
Clear Realization (Pervading Sentiment and Thought).
Our Original Teacher, Śākyamuni Buddha; May the assembly of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings in the Peacock Ocean confer auspiciousness. Mahāprajñāpāramitā.

I have heard that the *Peacock Vidyārājñī Sūtra* is so named because it expounds upon the causal origins of the Buddha-Mother (Bhagavatī), recites mantras against venomous snakes, and rescues sentient beings from calamities and hardships;
whatever is sought or requested, it accords with one's vows and intentions, and it provides for the arrangement of food and drink.

Each offered incense and flowers as an offering, each gave rise to joy, and all listened to the empowerment. Where this mantra was proclaimed, the four hundred and four diseases were entirely eliminated;
when these secret words were announced, ten thousand calamities and misfortunes were all utterly extinguished.

The gods of heaven, earth, and water, and the yakṣa deities, bowed their heads in refuge. The kings of mountains, the kings of dragons, the kings of rivers, and the great sages inclined their hearts in reverent admiration.

Rākṣasīs and women shall be unable to cause harm; yakṣa generals, may you all grant your blessings. May malefic stars be transformed into auspicious stars, and evil planets be converted into benevolent ones.
Public and private disputes shall vanish like melting ice; curses, enchantments, and toxic poisons shall dissipate like mist.
Those in office shall be pure, impartial, prosperous, and auspicious; those living at home shall enjoy blessings, longevity, health, and peace.

Whether old or young, all shall be secure and well; whether male or female, all shall rejoice. The majestic power of the Enlightened King pervades as many worlds as there are sands in the Ganges; it cannot be fully extolled, nor can its praise be exhausted.

Desiring to reveal the sacred texts of this great collection, one first invokes the auspicious names of the Seven Buddhas, so that the assembly may be honored without fatigue. Follow [the invocation].
The names of the Buddhas are: Paścimābhimukha, Mahāmāyūrī, Mahāmāyūrī-Śrīprabhāsa, and Māyūrī-Mahāmāyūrī.
Vidyārāja Buddha, Vidyārāja Buddha;
Jinyao Buddha on the southern face of the Snowy Mountains; Māhāmāyūrī Vidyārāja Buddha.
Emerging from Vulture Peak, revered by humans and devas, you traveled to the Deer Park and turned the Great Dharma Wheel. We look up to and praise your vast compassion.
May you graciously grant your clear testimony. On this occasion, as we recite the sutras and inaugurate the rites, we have intended to set forth our exposition.
We trust that within the Great Perfect Mirror, you will look upon us with clear discernment. Now, based on [the specific intent]:

On this very day, having washed my hands and burned incense, I prostrate before the Peacock-Arhat Śākyamuni, Teacher of the Snowy Mountains. I pray that you will extend your golden eyes and witness this humble petition.
On the [day] of the [month] year [year], I invite the assembly of monks to my home to make offerings to the Buddha, to bear witness, and to recite the scriptures. The Great Mother of Buddhas.
The Sutra of the Honored One, the Vidyārāja Kṣemaṅkara. Through the empowerment of the sacred text and its divine mantras, and by extolling his vast and magnificent name,

may the merit thus accumulated first be dedicated toward the vast *tathatā* (suchness) and the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), adorning the fruit of Buddhahood and Bodhi without artifice, and thereby repaying the profound kindness of the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
Thank you. Next, in response to the profound virtue of the Dragon Deities, we pray for the protection of the life-destiny star official of this current birth.
May its auspicious majesty and celestial form shine upon us; we only wish that Your Equal and True Compassion may likewise receive these merits, and together bestow blessings and auspiciousness.
We hope that henceforth our bodies shall be at peace and our lives long, that fortune may gather and calamities be dispelled. In... [end of fragment].

Within the Buddha’s light, may all be auspicious and favorable. Having thus expressed our sincere intentions above, we respectfully rely upon the venerable assembly to tirelessly exercise their compassionate grace by ringing the bells and reciting the *Buddhamātṛ Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī Sūtra*. [The preceding invocation is concluded.
(Upon the completion of the sūtra recitation).
One should offer all kinds of subtle and exquisite flowers,
incense, lamps, ointments, fruits, and other offerings, which arise from the causal nature of the gathering of all devas,
beginning with the invocation of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Śrī-Ārya-Mañjuśrī-Yamāntaka (the King of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel), up to the mantra *pūtra svāhā*.
I offer this to the Guru and the Triple Gem; may you, out of compassion, graciously accept it.
Oṃ sarvata-thāgata oṃ puṣpe dhūpe āloke gandhe naivedye pradīpe amṛta-samudra-sapūrṇa-samaya.
YA HŪṂ. We pay homage to the Buddha, the Sovereign Vidyārāja of Incense and Flowers.
Bound by the boundary, the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra brings forth auspiciousness.
Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the Great Heavenly King and Lord of the Eastern World,
who governs the gandharvas and forms the realm of yoga;
Virūḍhaka, the Great Heavenly King and Lord of the Southern World.
The Great Heavenly King Virūpākṣa, who governs the western world,
presides over the kumbhāṇḍas and binds the consecrated realm of the Lotus. He governs the great lords of the nāgas.
The Great Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa, Lord of the Northern World,
who governs the yakṣas and establishes the *karmadhātu* boundary;
and the Great Heavenly King Mahābrahmā, Lord of the Central World.
He who presides over the hosts of humans and devas, Having formed the Yoga Realm,
The Lord of the Eastern World, Whose name is the Buddha Akṣobhya, Proclaims sublime verses,
Forming the Vajra Realm.
The Lord of the Southern World, The Buddha named Ratnasambhava, Utters sublime verses, forming a lotus realm.
The Lord of the Northern World, The Buddha named Amoghasiddhi, Utters sublime verses.
Within the square world-system formed by the *karmabhūmi* boundary, the Buddha named Vairocana, the Honored One, proclaims sublime verses and establishes the *yogabhūmi* boundary.
I respectfully invoke the Buddha Akṣobhya of the East, Whose body is azure-blue and radiates light;
With hand-seal he grasps the *vajra* that subdues Māra. May all present with sincere resolve pay homage;
Now, circling the incense altar with secret mantras, We rely upon this to manifest the Vajradhātu.
We respectfully invoke the Buddha Ratnasambhava of the South, Whose body is crimson and radiates brilliant light;
Holding a mani-jewel in his hand-seal, The assembly, with sincere resolve, pays homage.
Now, circling the incense altar with secret mantras, We rely upon this to establish the consecration boundary.

I respectfully invoke Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter, Whose body is white and radiates brilliant light, Holding a wondrous lotus flower in the mudrā of his hand. With single-minded devotion, the assembly takes refuge and pays homage;
Now, reciting the secret mantras around the incense altar, We rely upon this to manifest the Lotus Realm.
I respectfully invite the Buddha of Northern Accomplishment, Whose body is black and radiates light, Holding the mudrā of the Sublime Demon-Subduer. May the assembly with sincere resolve pay homage;
Now, circling the incense altar with secret mantras, We rely upon this to establish the Karma-maṇḍala.
I respectfully invoke the Buddha Vairocana from the center, Whose body is yellow and radiates brilliant light;
Holding the hand-seal of the thousand-spoked wheel, The assembly now pays homage with a sincere mind.
Now, circling the incense altar with secret mantras, We rely upon this to establish the Yoga realm.
Gathering merit and welcoming auspiciousness, banners and streamers form a precious canopy; as golden bells tinkle, all the Akṣobhya,
Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Ratnasambhava,
and Vṛddhi [deities] are utterly extinguished.
Regarding these strange and monstrous phenomena: the compassion of the Tathāgata Amitābha Buddha is exceedingly vast. The Celestial King Virūpākṣa has arrived;
may he bring fulfillment to the Great Brahmā of Vairocana and Mañjuśrī.
Having bound the Lotus Realm—Vajra, Abhiṣeka, and Karma;
O Yoginīs, Devatās, Asuras, Yakṣas, and so forth (Mahāmāyūrī, Jvālāmālinī, etc.
who have come to hear the Dharma—you should listen with a resolute mind. (Namo Mahāmāhāmāyūrī).
The Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī Buddha (etcetera).
First Fascicle Complete. May there be peace and security.
Homage to the Great Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī Buddha. I take refuge in and pay homage to the Tathāgata. *Namaḥ mahāmāyūryai vidyārājñyai*. *Namo bhagavate tathāgatāya*.
The Yakṣa of the Middle Volume Presents Medicine; the Holy Assembly of Yakṣas Descends Auspiciousness and Hangs Golden Cords.
The true incense of precepts and meditative concentration sends its burning fragrance soaring to the heavens. With sincere devotion, the patron burns it in the golden censer;
in an instant, its swirling vapors pervade the ten directions. In days of yore, Yaśodharā relied upon it to escape peril and eliminate all obstacles.
The fragrance of the parasitic grass has just been incensed upon the burner; within the precious censer, sandalwood and milk-like incense are truly worthy offerings.

Auspicious clouds swirl as the lotuses quiver, and the Buddhas of the ten directions descend from their celestial palaces. The Arhats of Mount Qingliang come to receive offerings from the human realm.
The Buddha Vidyārāja; the yakṣa general Karkoṭaka; the yakṣa deity Pāṭali-hasta;
the yakṣa king Bhadra-karṇa, who dwells in the city of Sūttanu; and the great yakṣa Bhadraśila, who dwells in the city of Śrāvastī.
Qingjiang Yin:
Sandalwood incense from Niu-shou Mountain, As offerings, billowing auspicious clouds arise. Piercing upward into the Nine Heavens, They form a canopy of fragrant clouds.
I only pray that you will compassionately accept this with pity.
Waves wash away the sandalwood and milk incense; its fragrance is rich and pervasive. As the golden burner grows warm, its scent spreads throughout the ten directions.
In days of yore, Yaśodharā once escaped calamity; within the flames, her misfortunes were dispelled.

VII. Repentance and Petitionary Confession The Compassionate Lord within the three thousandfold world-systems of the Vidyārāja Buddhas, The Great Dharma King of the ten billion continents— May you all open your eyes of wisdom to behold the sentiments of ordinary beings;
Whatever the sentient beings seek, you shall respond to it all.

(Praise the Triple Gem. Humbly request their witness: For myself, as I recite this scripture today, and for my family and dependents, through this recitation of the scripture, [I pray] that all illnesses and sufferings within each person’s body may be removed, etc., and that they may all recover in peace and safety.
O King of Vidyārājas who can free one from the suffering of illness!
The Buddha abides within the true suchness of the dharma-realm; Formless and shapeless, free from all defilements, Sentient beings perceive his various bodies; All terrors are utterly removed.
He is able to eliminate terror; Terror and the source of terror are both entirely dispelled.
Untie the knots, untie the knots, untie the bonds of resentment;
Having untied them, may the resentments of many lifetimes and the karmic debts of enemies meet when they encounter one another; Meeting and encountering, may they rejoice together;
May these enemies and enemies each find mutual joy, Untying resentment and releasing the knots.
The power of the Vidyārāja Sūtra is inconceivable; It delivers sentient beings without end.
May the donor, with a sincere heart, take refuge and pay homage: All things that are not beneficial shall become beneficial;
Things that are not beneficial shall become vastly beneficial; Vastly beneficial.
With the forty-eight marks of supreme dignity and subtle beauty, cultivated through three great *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas,
his face is like the full moon and his eyes are like lotuses; all in heaven and among men revere him,
whereby poison and venom are transformed into nectar— transformed into nectar.
In the heavens above and the worlds below, there is none like the Buddha; throughout the ten directions, there is likewise no one to compare with him.
Having seen all that exists in the world, I find that among them, none is equal to the Buddha.
All other curses and incantations are entirely extinguished; one is able to remain free from such curses and incantations.
The first obstacle, the second speech, the third poisons and their transgressions; The four grave offenses, the five heinous crimes, the faults of the six sense organs;
The seven prohibitions and the eight difficulties—may these transgressions be dissolved and accepted. The nine fetters and the ten entanglements are all repented.
Repenting and eliminating karmic offenses. A five-character verse.
A red *uṣṇīṣa* upon the crown, like the sun reflecting off green mountains; Between the brows, a white *ūrṇā-kośa*, like the moon descending upon the blue sea.
I bow my head to the God among Gods, Who was born in the Lumbinī Garden, And pointed to heaven and earth with his fingers.
Taking seven steps upon red lotuses, the Ocean-Seal Samādhi is serene;
The light of compassion illuminates the ten directions; Because he extensively bestows the twelve vows, he is titled the King of the Dharma.
The Bodhisattva is like the cool moon, Like a jade mirror in the void; When the water of sentient beings' minds is pure, The Bodhisattva’s reflection appears therein.
Sins of a hundred kalpas and a thousand lifetimes Are swept away and eliminated in a single thought, Like a great fire consuming withered grass.
Exhaustively extinguished without remainder—
these four words describe the Buddha’s true Dharma-body, which is like empty space, manifesting forms in response to sentient beings.
Like the Great Perfection of Awakening within the moon reflected in water, you manifested your traces in the Western Continent of India; your mind encompasses the vast void,
its measure equaling the realms of the sands of the Ganges.
The Triple Gem of Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha is the field of merit for all sentient beings; in every prayer offered, its response is surely manifested.
The eternally abiding Triple Gem pervades the ten directions, responding according to the minds of sentient beings.
The mountain of the Buddha’s merits manifests in response to conditions— lofty indeed, towering indeed; the ocean of the Dharma and wisdom is most vast and most deep.
Rākṣasī! Rākṣasī hosts, may auspiciousness descend!
Rākṣasī hosts, may auspiciousness descend! Rākṣasī hosts, may great auspiciousness descend!
Rākṣasī hosts, may auspiciousness descend and calamities and obstacles be dispelled!
The assembly of Rāli women brings down great auspiciousness (in four even tones).
The holy assembly of nāga kings brings down auspiciousness:
the Buddha, the World-Honored One; the Nāga King; the Dragon-Tree King; the Brahmā Nāga King; and the Great Nāga King.
Indra, the Dragon King who Eliminates Obstacles and Calamities; Yama, the Dragon King who Ensures Peace and Security;
Madhukūṭapuṣpāhara, the Dragon King of the Buddha Bhagavān; Brahmā, the Dragon King; and Nāgavṛkṣarāja, the Bodhisattva Dragon King.
To the Dragon King Yama, the Dragon King Mahāsamudra, the Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna,
the Deva Qingjiangyin, the Yakṣa Āsvala, and all others who have come to hear the Dharma, you should listen with a sincere and resolute mind.
The Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī Sūtra: Entreaty for the Buddha to Act as Witness of Great Compassion; Saving from Suffering and Delivering from Calamity;
Amidst the Moonlight upon the Waters with a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes; Beside the Rock of Potalaka, upon a Single-Leaf Skiff.
The White-Robed One of Wondrous Appearance, amidst the Purple Bamboo Grove, within the waves of the wind,
fulfilling all wishes according to one's heart;
the Golden Letter Sutra.

Devas, asuras, yakṣas, and others who come to hear the Dharma should apply their minds with sincerity to the Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī Sūtra and the Greatly Compassionate and Merciful Avalokiteśvara’s Mantra for Eliminating Calamities and Obstacles: Oṃ māṇi padme hūṃ.
May the celestial asuras, yakṣas, and others who have come to hear the Dharma,
together with the Peacock-Vidyārājñī and the Buddha Vidyārāja, eliminate calamities, prolong life, and preserve peace and security.
The Middle Volume is Complete; May There Be Peace and Security (as before).
Up to the Seven Buddhas: May the Tathāgata Vipaśyin bring down auspiciousness.
Majestic Great Dharma King, The light from his ūrṇā-kośa illuminates the great trichiliocosm. Unshakable by the eight winds.
A single lotus of purple-gold, Śikhin Tathāgata (as before).
His marks and signs are of true golden color; his boundless, pure Dharma-body, with a serene countenance, ascends the precious throne.
The moon from the ocean-treasury rises in the sky: Viśvabhū Tathāgata.
Lord of Compassion for the World, Great Dharma King as numerous as motes of dust and sands, may all that is sought fulfill its vow;
may your eye of wisdom discern the sentiments of ordinary beings.
Your physical form is like a mountain of gold, most upright and majestic, exceedingly subtle and wondrous, like pure lapis lazuli.
Within, there appears the image of true gold; the countenance of Kāśyapa-Muni is most wondrous.
Its radiance illuminates the ten directions. I have previously made offerings to him, and now I come once more to behold him in person—Tathāgata Kāśyapa.
To the Holy Lord, King of Devas, With the voice of the kalaviṅka bird, Who has compassion for all sentient beings— To him we now pay homage.
I, Śākyamuni Tathāgata, pray that by this merit, It may reach all beings without exception: Both ourselves and all other sentient beings.
All together shall attain the Buddha-way.
The Seven Buddhas: King of the Gaṅgā River, King of the Sindhu River, King of the Vakṣu River, and King of the Mahāvakṣu River.
Sita River King, Destroyer of Calamities and Obstacles; Malapa River King;
Sumeru Mountain King; Oṃ Ma Hūṃ, Snowy Mountain King;
Oṃ Ma Ni Hūṃ, Gandhamādana Mountain King; Oṃ Ma Ni Phaṭ Mi Hūṃ.
Bai-feng Shan-wang hu oṃ maṇi padme hūṃ. Constellations:
entering the Qingjiang Yin, there are twenty-eight constellations. Namo to the Buddha Akṣobhya of the East.
In the south is known as Ratnasaṃbhava; In the west is Amitābha and the rest; In the north is the Honored One of Accomplishment.

Homage to the Buddha Vairocana of the Central Direction. May the thousand Buddhas of the Constellation Kalpa, And the deities of the seven lunar mansions, Grant their protective grace. Homage to the Buddha King of Great Blazing Light.
I look up and entreat the Radiance of the Blazing Extinguisher of Calamities, Who leads all the constellations down from the celestial palace.
The twenty-eight lunar mansions are arrayed left and right, With the twelve zodiac signs arranged in two rows;
The seven mansions of the eastern gate stand forth.
The stars and constellations of the central heavens and the Southern Dipper, the arrayed luminaries of the forest of stars and the multitude of True Ones—
those who can give rise to a sincere heart to seek repentance will have calamities extinguished and blessings converge upon them.
[The Seven Mansions of the Southern Gate.]
The Milky Way is deep and vast, illuminated by the light of the hare-marked moon; The Sun of Wisdom rises majestically, shining brilliantly through the great void.
The Sea of Blessings flows on like a profound crossing; The Mountain of Longevity looms high, equal to Mount Sumeru.
The Seven Mansions of the Western Gate.
The Sun, the stars and constellations, the Great Void (Tai-xiang), The Lords of Virtue of Metal, Wood, Water, Fire, and Earth,
Zi-qi, Luo-hou, and Yue-bei, The annual flow, the ten-year cycles, and the natal hour,
The seven mansions of the Northern Gate.

Jiǎo (Jiao), Kāng (Kang), Dǐ (Di), Fáng (Fang), Xīn (Xin), Wěi (Wei), Jī (Ji); Dǒu (Dou), Niú (Niu), Nǚ (Nü), Xū (Xu), Wēi (Wei), Shì (Shi), Bì (Bi), Kuí (Kui), Lóu (Lou), Wèi (Wei), Mǎo (Mao), Bì (Bi), Zǐ (Zi), Shēn (Shen);
Jǐng (Jing), Guǐ (Gui), Liǔ (Liu), Xīng (Xing), Zhāng (Zhang), Yì (Yi), Zhěn (Zhen)—the twenty-eight lunar mansions.
The Buddha Ānanda is wondrous and immeasurable; The three volumes of the True Commentary are widely proclaimed.
May the twenty-eight lunar mansions increase one’s years of longevity, And may the twelve palaces and celestial stems bring peace and security, As well as the nine luminaries and the governing stars.
The myriad phenomena in their array dispel calamities and obstacles; The stars and constellations fill the heavens, descending auspicious blessings.
From this day forth, as the lay patrons recite the sutras, Their mountain of longevity towers high and their fortune extends far and wide.
The stars and constellations fill the heavens.

The first line refers to companions of the immortals; the second line refers to companions of the immortals who possess the five supernatural powers (*pañcābhijñā*); the third line refers to companions of the immortals who have attained the Way while possessing the five supernatural powers;
the fourth line refers to companions of the immortals who have attained the Way with the great five supernatural powers reaching even into poisonous drugs.
One phrase is poison; two phrases are the deity of poison; three phrases are great poison; four phrases are the two Bodhisattvas, Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata, and the Three Jewels.
[This concludes] the "Introduction to the Clear River."
I bow my head in refuge to the Buddha, seated upon a jeweled terrace in the celestial palace;
may you who are longed for by sentient beings descend early to be born among us. I take refuge and pay homage to the Tathāgata, Maitreya.
I bow my head in refuge to the Dharma, which possesses the three knowledges and six supernormal powers, opening the treasury of sūtras as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
The Seal of Mind that Upholds the Dharanis is compliant; Neither going nor coming.

I bow my head in refuge to the Sangha, the treasury of the ocean. Possessing the three insights and the six supernormal powers, May we meet at the three assemblies as personally prophesied on Vulture Peak. Field of Merit.
I prostrate to the Sangha, the Triple Gem, the excellent field of merit for all sentient beings;
those who can take refuge in them shall obtain boundless blessings.
To the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha—the Triple Gem—and to Mahāmāyūrī, the Mother of Buddhas, the Vidyārājñī Sūtra: I now pay homage with my life.
Sins are extinguished and the source of merit increases.
Mahāmāyūrī, devas, asuras, yakṣas, and so forth—(Oṃ Hūṃ). Come, Hūṃ! O Dharma-practitioner (Oṃ Hūṃ), you should apply your mind with sincerity—Hūṃ Oṃ Māni Hūṃ.
First, I repay the heavens and the earth; Second, I repay the sun and the moon.
Third, to repay the king; fourth, to repay one’s father and mother.
May these superior causes and conditions cause the three obstructions to be extinguished.
Mahāprajñā Rūpikā Vidyārājñī Buddha.
The third volume is complete; may there be peace and security.
Homage to the Buddha Mahāmāyūrīvidyārājñī.
Submitted by Qingzhen Baoge Chan Temple under the Sangha Office of Tongxiang County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang Province.

The Śramaṇa Huiri, who repays the Buddha’s kindness, has donated funds to commission the continued transcription of six copies of the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra* (the Honored Peacock Scripture). By the merit of this work, may his late father, Mr.
Jiang [name], surnamed Wang, be reborn early in the grade of the gods.
Copied on the [day] of the final month of the thirtieth year of the Jiajing era.
